props.title: The Poseidon Adventure
props.initialSlug: Passengers fight to survive in capsized luxury liner

sections.content: **The Poseidon Adventure** (1972) revolutionized disaster films, setting the template for star-studded survival epics. Gene Hackman leads an ensemble cast as a rebellious preacher guiding survivors through an upturned luxury liner after a massive wave hits on New Year's Eve. The film's practical effects and upside-down sets created a claustrophobic intensity that later inspired **Titanic** (1997) and **Deep Impact** (1998). Producer Irwin Allen became known as "The Master of Disaster" after this film's success, leading to **The Towering Inferno** (1974) and launching the 1970s disaster movie boom. movies.title: The Towering Inferno
movies.slug: Paul Newman and Steve McQueen battle a skyscraper fire in this intense disaster epic

sections.content: The film's influence extends beyond its immediate era. **Airport** (1970) had proven audiences would flock to disaster films with multiple storylines, but Poseidon's focus on a core group fighting impossible odds became the new standard. This formula appears in modern disaster films like **San Andreas** (2015) and **2012** (2009), where personal drama drives the spectacle. The practical effects work - flooding real sets, dangerous stunts, and minimal optical effects - created a tangible danger that CGI-heavy modern films struggle to match.

The religious undertones and moral questions raised by Hackman's character influenced later disaster films like **Deep Impact** (1998) and **Knowing** (2009), where faith and science collide during catastrophic events. The film's confined setting and pressure-cooker atmosphere inspired submarine thrillers like **The Abyss** (1989) and **Crimson Tide** (1995). movies.title: The Day After Tomorrow
movies.slug: A climatologist races to save his son when global warming triggers a new ice age

sections.content: Contemporary filmmakers continue drawing from Poseidon's playbook. **Greenland** (2020) and **Geostorm** (2017) follow its template of personal stories amid global catastrophe. The film's innovative upside-down sets influenced **Inception** (2010) and **Tenet** (2020), where altered physics create similar visual challenges. The 2006 remake **Poseidon** proved the enduring appeal of the concept, though it relied more on digital effects than practical stunts.
